source_review.notes: Checked current Trino EXPLAIN, EXPLAIN ANALYZE, Web UI, JMX, and OpenMetrics documentation; current Spark monitoring, Web UI, and SQL performance documentation; current Flink metrics and backpressure documentation; current OpenTelemetry database-span conventions; and current Linux kernel TCP-counter and iproute2 ss documentation. All thirteen final references returned HTTP 200. Product/tool behavior is attributed, and causal guidance distinguishes direct evidence, inference, and controlled intervention.

evidence: Reviewed lifecycle intervals, stage DAG, critical path, estimate/actual rows and bytes, Q-error, task metric vectors, tail ratios, and exchange byte/rate notation.
Reviewed logical partitions, selected attempts, plan epochs, endpoints, intervals, producer/wire/receiver/consumer bytes, and causal-chain notation.
Checked matching units/scopes, positive-denominator conditions, explicit zero handling, distribution sample counts, and overlap qualifications.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Elapsed wall time, task/CPU work, blocked time, logical bytes, wire bytes, and node-wide counters remain distinct.

evidence: Executed the Python 3 fixture and reproduced q_error=25.0, median_task_seconds=44, skew_ratio=4.77, lifecycle_seconds=270, and execution_share_percent=88.9.
Recomputed the five-task example median as 44 seconds and 210/44 as approximately 4.77.
Recomputed Exercise 2 Q-error as 90, six-task median as 34 seconds, and 198/34 as approximately 5.82.
numerical_recomputation.notes: Q-error and tail ratios prioritize investigation; they do not identify mechanism without aligned operator, attempt, and infrastructure evidence.

evidence: Verified non-overlapping lifecycle components sum to query wall time only under one documented boundary contract.
Verified Q=max(a/e,e/a) is symmetric for positive reciprocal multiplicative over/underestimates and requires separate zero cases.
Verified stage dependency/overlap determines latency while summed task durations measure work, and exchange byte conservation is semantic rather than raw equality.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: Critical-path relevance, causal mechanism, intervention response, and fleet value are separate conclusions.

evidence: Reviewed estimate/actual zeros, few-task percentile misuse, tiny/huge files, compressed expansion, many-to-many output, hot keys, and adaptive discarded work.
Reviewed equal work with GC/disk/network delay, unequal work with normal infrastructure, upstream backpressure, client drain, source throttle, cluster contention, and cache effects.
Reviewed retries, speculation, losing attempts, stale/final-only plans, clock/interval mismatch, incomplete sampling, sensitive telemetry, and multi-setting interventions.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Evidence gaps retain competing hypotheses; wrong results, policy violations, corruption, or unsafe collection trigger containment.

evidence: Traced query/fingerprint, parameters/snapshot, plan epochs, logical nodes, stages, exchanges, logical partitions, selected attempts, workers, sources, endpoints, and client through one timeline.
Checked estimate/actual node/units/scope matching, attempt-aware useful/wasted work, stage dependency overlap, backpressure direction, and endpoint/time attribution.
Checked interventions preserve correctness, vary one bounded factor, use matched controls, record configuration/cohort, and retain rollback.
invariant_checking.notes: Plan, operator, scheduler, runtime, storage, network, connector, client, and cluster evidence are correlated without collapsing ownership.

evidence: Reviewed the ten-step plan-to-network audit from symptom/evidence preservation through topology, estimates, attempts, flow control, infrastructure, intervention, and durable remediation.
Checked the causal-sufficiency chain from plan/input condition to operator state, task/exchange behavior, resource symptom, and query outcome.
Checked why exchange wait does not establish network causality and why correlated flow/path evidence plus predicted intervention strengthens the claim.
proof_review.notes: Findings are labeled by evidence strength, include counterevidence, and do not claim universal root cause from one metric.

evidence: Audited query fingerprint/instance, lifecycle, critical path, estimate error, stage/fragment, task attempt, skew, backpressure, network symptom, and causal intervention terminology.
Confirmed logical/physical/final adaptive plans, fragments/stages/exchanges, partitions/attempts, busy/idle/blocked/backpressured, and source/client wait are differentiated.
Confirmed plan cause, resource mechanism, symptom, correlation, controlled intervention, workaround, and durable remediation are not conflated.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: Every diagnostic label carries scope, interval, units, attempt lineage, and claim strength where relevant.

evidence: Reviewed lifecycle, critical path, rows/bytes, task distributions, CPU/block/memory/spill/GC/disk, exchange queues/rates, RTT/loss/retransmits, source, client, concurrency, tails, and fleet cost.
Confirmed no universal Q-error, skew ratio, percentile, throughput, retransmission, queue, partition, memory, timeout, or intervention threshold is prescribed.
Confirmed remediation claims require matched snapshots/config/load, exact result checks, multiple samples/cohorts, predicted signature, rollback, and post-change fleet verification.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: One fast rerun, high average, isolated counter, final plan, or dashboard screenshot is not mislabeled causal proof.

conceptual_review.notes: Reviewed symptom definition, evidence preservation, lifecycle, executed plan/revisions, critical path, estimate errors, task/attempt distributions, backpressure, scans, stateful operators, exchanges, workers/runtime, network, client, concurrency, hypotheses, interventions, and handoff.

practitioner_review.notes: Reviewed implementable query-to-endpoint identifiers, machine-readable artifact exports, lifecycle boundaries, stage DAGs, attempt-aware quantiles, flow-control walks, peer-worker comparisons, socket/NIC/path escalation, matched cohorts, one-factor tests, claim-strength labels, redaction, checksums, rollback, ownership, and verification. Internal practitioner-oriented review only.

pedagogical_review.notes: Verified progression from symptom and evidence through plan, stages/tasks, operators/exchange, hosts/network/client, causal testing, and handoff. Ten examples and five answered exercises cover lifecycle, estimate error, skew classification, backpressure, client drain, network correlation, metadata overhead, AQE waste, intervention, executable metrics, full evidence design, competing chains, escalation, and reporting.

limitations: Internal evidence record only; no external Trino/Spark/Flink/OpenTelemetry/Linux/iproute2 maintainer, query-engine operator, database/distributed-systems/OS/runtime/storage/network/platform/SRE/performance/security specialist, incident responder, affected user, governance or accessibility specialist, or certification review is claimed.
